content:
maya: Quick handoff note — I'm seeing a noisy kv-cache-latency alert firing across a subset of small-model servers in us-west-2. It's paging at night and looks like batcher jitter after a quantize job started earlier. No 5xx errors reported, customer-facing requests are still succeeding, but p95 token gen for tiny models has jumped for a few hosts.

oncall-bot: Alert triggered: kv-cache-latency (prod/us-west-2) — 120 instances over 5m. Pager: oncall@redwood. Severity: page. Link: https://metrics.redwood/alerts/kv-cache-latency

jon: Can you confirm this is correlated with the quantize run? Any config or infra deploys recently? :eyes:

maya: No infra deploys. The quantize batch started ~30m before alerts. I pulled kernel CPU and nvtx traces — spikes line up with the batcher flush. I want to avoid waking the rotation for noise. Proposal: temporarily raise the alert threshold from 200ms -> 300ms and silence paging for 30m while we validate. Estimated SLO impact: current p95 baseline ~180ms, bumping threshold will let p95 drift to ~220ms in worst-case for affected hosts; global SLO is 250ms so we remain within SLO.

lee: If you do that, please keep channel notifications (no pager) and add a runbook note. I'll take primary if this escalates. Also leave the alert on dashboards so folks can watch.

maya: Doing the change now. Steps I'm running:

```yaml
# alert-manager rule snippet
- alert: kv-cache-latency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kv_cache_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool)) > 0.3
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

I'll update `for` from 5m -> 10m and set expr threshold to 0.4 (approx 300ms equivalent).

Command I'm using to silence the pager:

```bash
amtool silence --matcher 'alertname=kv-cache-latency' --duration 30m --comment 'temporary: validate quantize impact during handoff'
```

oncall-bot: Silence created by maya (expires in 30m). Silence ID: s-08a3f.

sam: +1 to silencing for validation window. Also recommend we create a routing fallback for tiny-models to the secondary pool so external customers see less tail impact. I can push an emergency route override:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/internal/routing/override \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"model":"small-*","route":"pool-secondary","duration":"60m","reason":"temp mitigation for kv-cache jitter"}'
```

jon: Good call. What's our rollback plan if this causes unanticipated load on pool-secondary?

maya: If pool-secondary CPU or queue depth increases >80% or error rate >0.1% we revert override. I'll set an automation check to auto-revert and page if thresholds hit. Leaving the runbook pointer below for next shift: https://runbooks.redwood/latency/kv-cache-jitter — includes tracing, query to identify hosts, and commands to drain a host.

lee: I'll monitor dashboards for the next 45m. If things look stable, mark ready for handoff to night rotation. Also note: add a remediation tag to the git issue so PMs see we're tracking.

maya: Done — updated alert rule, created silence, and pushed a temporary slack-only notification. Also added a short incident note in the support ticket: "Investigating kv-cache jitter correlated with quantize job; temporary alert threshold increase and routing override in place; watching SLOs."

sam: I applied the routing override and set automation to revert on high load.

maya: Current status: paging silenced for 30m, threshold bumped, routing override active for 60m. Monitoring: p95 across global small-models = 215ms, error rate unchanged at 0.02%. If any of these change to error_rate>0.1% or p95>250ms I'll unmute and escalate.

oncall-bot: Note: Silence expires in 18m.

maya: Handoff notes for the next oncall —
- primary: lee (will monitor dashboards)
- secondary: jon (ready to help with pool capacity)
- runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/latency/kv-cache-jitter
- actions taken: threshold increased, silence 30m, routing override to pool-secondary 60m, automation revert on load>80% or err_rate>0.1%
- acceptance criteria to close this thread: 45m stable window with p95<240ms and error_rate<0.05% and no new host-level CPU saturation alerts.

If you pick this up lee, please snapshot the dashboard and paste link before closing. Thanks — I'm leaving the channel but reachable if it needs escalation. :headphones:

lee: Got it. I'll watch and ping if anything changes. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — will follow up in the morning with root-cause notes if we confirm quantize correlation.
